title: Recording, mixing, editing: Nineteen Hundred And Eighty Five, Picasso’s Last Words (Drink To Me) by Wings | 1973
content:
Studio Three, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Geoff Emerick

The Band On The Run songs ‘Nineteen Hundred And Eighty Five’ and ‘Picasso’s Last Words (Drink To Me)’ were mixed in stereo on 28 October 1973.

This was a late-night session starting at 8pm, and followed the cover photography session for the album. The session ended at 6.45am the following morning.

There was a last-minute overdub for ‘Nineteen Hundred And Eighty Five’. Paul McCartney decided to re-record his lead vocals for the song, which had the working title ‘Piano Thing – 1985’. The song was then mixed, with the final version being an edit of RS5 and RS8.

The last song to be mixed on this day – and, indeed, for the album, was ‘Picasso’s Last Words (Drink To Me)’. Studio engineer Geoff Emerick added elements from an effects tape, prepared at his request by Theatre Projects Sound Limited. It included dialogue from Le Flash Touristique, a BBC French Language Service recording, along with party noises and laughter.

The mix was one of the more complex for the album, and took 14 attempts to complete. The final version was an edit of RS13 and RS14.

Towards the end of the session, Emerick also crossfaded a snippet of ‘Band On The Run’, adding it to the end of ‘Nineteen Hundred And Eighty Five’ to bookend the album.

Band On The Run was never really designed to be a concept album, but Paul obviously liked the idea: that’s why he had me edit little snatches of melodies from other songs and snippets of French dialogue into ‘Picasso’s Last Words’. He also came up with the suggestion of creating a reprise of the title track to end the album. It wasn’t a new recording – we just flew in a section of the original version, and it worked just fine.
Geoff Emerick
Here, There and Everywhere: My Life Recording The Music Of The Beatles
